elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: 5 methods - (1) In-person data collection visits at 3 sites (Birmingham, San Diego, Seattle) lasting 2.5-4 hours with >10 data domains; (2) Electronic health record screening for ages 40+ (2020-2025 encounters) using ICD-10 codes E11.X (T2DM) and R73.09 (pre-diabetes); (3) Wave-based recruitment with monitoring/adjustment for balance, enrollment July 18, 2023 to November 30, 2026; (4) Home-based wearable monitoring (Dexcom G6 CGM, Garmin VivoSmart 5, environmental sensors) over 10-day periods; (5) Biospecimen collection (53 mL blood, urine) with standardized processing and UAB CCTS biobanking
sub_elements.quality_note: Detailed collection settings with specific sites, timeframes, protocols, and equipment. Replication feasible from provided information

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: 12 detailed methods - (1) Survey/questionnaire via REDCap (demographics, medical history, CES-D-10, PAID, RxNorm medications); (2) Physical measurements (height, weight, waist/hip, BP, HR); (3) Retinal imaging (7 devices: Aurora IQ, EIDON, Spectralis, Maestro2, Triton, Cirrus 5000, FLIO) with DICOM output; (4) Visual function (EVA, Mars chart, Topcon KR 800); (5) Clinical labs (CBC, NT-proBNP, Troponin-T, lipids, HbA1c, urine albumin); (6) ECG (Philips Pagewriter TC30); (7) Cognitive (MoCA Duo on iPad); (8) Peripheral neuropathy (10g monofilament); (9) CGM (Dexcom G6, 5-min intervals, 10 days); (10) Activity (Garmin VivoSmart 5, .FIT); (11) Environmental (custom sensor, 11 measures); (12) Biospecimens (plasma, serum, buffy coats, PBMCs, PAXgene RNA, urine)
sub_elements.quality_note: Comprehensive acquisition documentation with specific device models, software, measurement protocols, and output formats. Supports reproducibility

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, and Labeling Strategies
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: 5 items - (1) Data standardization/harmonization across 3 sites via SOPs, common protocols, REDCap, standardized training with certification, Manual of Procedures; (2) Image format conversion (proprietary .fda/.sdt → DICOM, .FIT → mHealth); (3) Biospecimen processing (standardized local processing, centralized PBMC at UAB CCTS, batch shipping to UW NORC, genomic DNA extraction); (4) Quality control (training certification, equipment calibration, duplicate measurements, REDCap validation, practice subjects); (5) Data mapping to standards (OMOP CDM, DICOM, mHealth, RxNorm, ICD-10); cleaning_strategies: Multi-site harmonization via standardized protocols, common equipment, REDCap, FAIR principles, pilot enrollment (July-Nov 2023) for coordinator familiarization
sub_elements.quality_note: Detailed preprocessing and cleaning with standardization procedures, format conversions, QC measures, and standards mapping. Labeling strategies not explicitly present but RxNorm/ICD-10 coding mentioned

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.evidence: REDCap (data management, surveys, recruitment interface); Dexcom G6 (CGM); Garmin VivoSmart 5 (activity); 7 retinal imaging devices (Aurora IQ, EIDON, Spectralis HRA OCT, Maestro2 3D OCT-1, Triton DRI OCT, Cirrus 5000, FLIO); Electronic Visual Acuity tester (M&S Technology); Mars chart (Mars Perceptrix); Topcon KR 800 (autorefraction); Philips Pagewriter TC30 (ECG); MoCA Duo Application (iPad); Environmental sensor (Karalis Johnson Retina Center, UW)
